evidence_updates.observation: A disposable local counterexample showed PYTHONSAFEPATH/-P can coexist with a poisoned PYTHONPATH that wins module resolution; python -I rejected that injected path. Target main 1243bd31606df1d52e1865fd7f1cf5d563c499d8 changes three security-sensitive verifier entry points to python3 -I - while leaving the controlled inner import experiment non-isolated.
evidence_updates.nonclaim: The whole two-job workflow is not complete, and isolated import-path shape does not bind module origin, bytes, hash, or manifest.

evidence_updates.observation: A disposable Linux burst spawned 256 processes but observed only 8 unique /proc start ticks, with up to 44 distinct PIDs sharing one tick. Thus process_start_ticks alone is empirically non-unique on that lane.
evidence_updates.candidate: Bind host_boot_id + process_pid + process_start_ticks + ProductStart generation.
evidence_updates.nonclaim: Composite equality does not authenticate upstream receipts or prove accepted-Hostinger ProductStart identity.

evidence_updates.observation: A disposable SQLite counterworld committed a marker visible through WAL while the main database file device/inode/size/hash remained unchanged; copying only the main file lost the committed marker.
evidence_updates.primary_support: SQLite documents the WAL as containing committed transactions not yet applied to the main database.
evidence_updates.nonclaim: No accepted Hostinger Frank database was opened or mutated; no productive restart/readback was executed.

evidence_updates.observation: A local same-filesystem hardlink fixture showed O_NOFOLLOW accepts both names of the same inode, while an st_nlink==1 candidate denied the multi-link state and re-accepted after rollback.
evidence_updates.nonclaim: st_nlink==1 does not close parent-directory replacement, ownership, post-check, or complete hardlink attack surfaces.

primary_sources.title: Python 3.13 command-line and environment documentation
primary_sources.support: -P suppresses an implicitly prepended unsafe path, PYTHONPATH separately augments sys.path, and -I implies -E, -P and -s while ignoring PYTHON* environment variables.

primary_sources.title: SQLite WAL-mode file format
primary_sources.support: The WAL records committed transactions not yet applied to the main database.

primary_sources.title: Linux proc_pid_stat(5)
primary_sources.support: Field 22 is process start time after boot in clock ticks; the specification does not define it as a unique process identifier.

primary_sources.title: Python os.stat_result documentation
primary_sources.support: st_nlink records the number of hard links and fstat observes metadata of the opened descriptor.

hypotheses.claim: Security-sensitive Python receipts require both environment isolation and post-import artifact authority; -I blocks ambient PYTHON* influence but cannot prove the imported module is the approved artifact.
hypotheses.test: Run a matrix covering PYTHONPATH, user site, sitecustomize, .pth, symlinks, zip imports and loader hooks, then require every critical import to resolve under an allowlisted root with content hash and manifest membership.
hypotheses.falsifier: An isolated interpreter alone rejects all preregistered artifact substitution paths and cryptographically identifies approved module bytes without an additional origin/hash manifest gate.

hypotheses.claim: A process receipt cohort must bind boot ID, PID and start ticks together; start ticks alone are insufficient, while the tuple remains a discriminator rather than receipt authentication.
hypotheses.test: Exercise same-tick/different-PID, PID-reuse, reboot, namespace and copied-field controls with independently observed tuple fields.
hypotheses.falsifier: Tick-only identity remains collision-free across preregistered high-concurrency and reboot/PID-reuse trials.

hypotheses.claim: UnifiedDB continuity must be demonstrated by a cohort-bound nonce and semantic epoch written through the admitted connection and read after authorized restart; neither main-file identity nor a long-lived WAL hash is sufficient.
hypotheses.test: Write nonce+epoch, test pre/post-checkpoint restart, and require readback while stale-main, separated-WAL, rollback, downgrade and library-swap controls fail closed.
hypotheses.falsifier: Main-file identity alone reliably distinguishes every committed, rolled-back, stale and WAL-separated state across the preregistered matrix.

hypotheses.claim: For a unique-file credential contract, O_NOFOLLOW plus descriptor-based type/mode/owner/parent checks and st_nlink==1 is stronger than O_NOFOLLOW alone, but still requires an explicit deployment identity policy.
hypotheses.test: Test legitimate deployment rollouts, hardlink aliases, parent swaps, rename races, bind mounts and post-open mutation on a disposable lane.
hypotheses.falsifier: The strict single-link policy rejects required legitimate deployment patterns without a safer equivalent identity contract, or accepts an unauthorized alias/control state.

counterhypotheses.counterevidence: safe_path=true coexisted with CWD reintroduced through dot and empty PYTHONPATH segments.
256 processes produced 8 unique ticks; maximum 44 PIDs shared one tick.
A WAL-only committed marker existed while main-file identity was unchanged.

new_concepts.name: Environment-to-Artifact Closure
new_concepts.definition: A two-stage receipt: first eliminate ambient interpreter authority, then bind every consequential import to approved origin bytes and a manifest.

new_concepts.name: Process Generation Coordinate
new_concepts.definition: The tuple host_boot_id, PID and process start ticks, scoped to one independently observed ProductStart generation.

new_concepts.name: Semantic Restart Witness
new_concepts.definition: A run-owned database nonce and semantic epoch whose successful post-restart readback proves state continuity more directly than storage-file metadata.

new_concepts.name: Receipt Cohort Closure
new_concepts.definition: One authenticated join across ProductStart, process coordinate, runtime/artifact identity, exact database object, semantic commit and successor restart generation.
